axisDefinitions.answerStatus: Response text only, judged against evaluation/questions.json and the README. Applies to all 35 results. Extra returned sources are never counted here.
axisDefinitions.sourceTraceabilityStatus: Technical provenance: every nonblank chunkId must exist in this run's manifest and its documentName must match the chunk metadata. A result with no returned source has no identifier that can be invalid, so it is PASS on this axis.
axisDefinitions.sourceCoverageStatus: For every material claim the answer uses to satisfy the rubric there must be at least one returned chunk that directly supports it. An exact refusal with no sources is PASS only for a genuinely unsupported question and FAIL for a supported one.
axisDefinitions.sourcePrecision: Measured, not a verdict. Every returned chunkId is classified individually in classifiedSources. direct = the chunk substantiates a named material claim, which is quoted in its note; contextual = the chunk is a substantive policy section on topic for the question but supports no claim the answer makes; irrelevant = unrelated to question and answer, or a heading-only stub that carries no body text and therefore can substantiate nothing. precisionAtK = (direct + contextual) / returned, null when nothing was returned.
axisDefinitions.readmeScope: Which README obligation the result exercises: core-contract (gpt-4o at the shipped default configuration), model-comparison (the generator-choice subtask), experiment-default-config (an Experiments & Edge Cases case whose variant is the default configuration), or experiment-variant (a deliberately non-default configuration).
axisDefinitions.requirementStatus: The README verdict, present for every result except an experiment-variant. FAIL for a wrong, incomplete or unsupported answer, a false refusal, missing evidence coverage, an invalid source, a malformed structured response or a broken lifecycle. Tallied per readmeScope and never as one combined figure.
axisDefinitions.fiveBulletSummaryRule: PASS requires exactly five bullets, no preface or conclusion, every bullet grounded in the corpus, no two bullets restating the same policy guidance, and every bullet stating a security topic. Guideline ownership, approval and review responsibility is document governance metadata, not a security theme.
